rows.assessment: Kamiguri et al. 2012, PMID:27857602, PMCID:PMC5070450, printed page 3, Results and Discussion first paragraph, left column. Direct contiguous PDF match with whitespace-only line-wrap normalization and actual typeset passage inspected; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. Junko Kamiguri is the first author; the running header says Hashimoto et al. Living source-named Vorticella sp. from activated sludge attached to glass rods was stimulated by hitting the dish; eight cells were observed at 6000 frames/s. Figures 3 and 5 show coiling and decreased end-to-end extension. The same paragraph says contour length does not change. All nine main-paper pages were inspected; raw videos were not reanalyzed. Model fits are not molecular proof. The primary PDF came from J-STAGE; an acquisition-helper failure left no original request timestamp or header receipt. Those missing fields are not reconstructed. Current taxonomic and culture identities remain unresolved.

rows.assessment: Ryu et al. 2012, PMID:23009835, PMCID:PMC3433611, printed page 862, Figure 2A caption, sentence beginning The stalk contraction. Direct contiguous PDF match and actual typeset passage inspected; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The primary PDF was retrieved from the Vanderbilt Lang Lab mirror. Source-named Vorticella convallaria contracted in microfluidic channels under varied flow and viscosity. Four to five contractions per cell per condition are not independent cells. Figure 3 uses six cells; Figure 4C uses fifteen in a separate analysis. Isometric force is extrapolated through a hydrodynamic model, not directly measured zero-shortening force. All eight main-paper pages and actual Figures 1-5 were inspected; the supplement was not. Projection and geometry assumptions remain relevant. Some extracted micrometre symbols appear as mm; no such numeric extraction is quoted. Culture/taxonomy correspondence is unresolved. No universal rate, force, calcium threshold, ATP independence or protein mechanism follows.

allocation.label: stalk contraction
allocation.definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell actively reduces the end-to-end extension of its stalk.

parent.label: cell body or cytoplasmic projection contraction
parent.inference: End-to-end contraction of the cell stalk is a narrower projection-contraction endpoint. The stalk includes an intracellular spasmoneme and a sheath; the entire sheath is not called cytoplasm.

historical_inspections.part_i_assessment: All nine typeset pages have now been read/visually inspected across the earlier and this follow-up. Printed p.3 Results distinguishes unchanged length along the stalk from decreasing extension during coiling. Figure 8/Table 2 show eight source-labelled cell profiles with fitted stretched-exponential parameters; Figure 9 compares fits and Figure 10 is a proposed model, not molecular proof. No universal speed or contour-shortening claim is accepted.
historical_inspections.part_ii_assessment: All nine typeset pages were inspected in this follow-up. Printed p.13 Experiments reports two cells, each used for two polymer types, with repeated measurements. Figure 3 shows observed reduced-length traces and model fits with shifted display time origins, not a continuous common time series. Printed p.16 distinguishes projection artifacts when the zooid rises in dense Ficoll from actual length change; recalculated values in Figure 7 use a geometric correction. Neither fitted rates nor viscosity exponents establish a universal trait threshold or molecular mechanism.

historical_inspections.assessment: Figure 2 directly shows contracted stalks and time-dependent projected lengths under varied viscosity and flow. Methods record 4-5 contractions per cell and condition, with rest periods and exclusion of abnormal contractions. Figure 3 reports six cells; Figure 4C reports fifteen. These are different analysis scopes, not independent replicates per trace. Figure 1 defines projection geometry. Isometric force is extrapolated with hydrodynamic assumptions, not directly measured at zero shortening. Figure 5 is a conceptual model, not molecular proof. The paper supports an observed stalk-contraction phenotype, not a universal rate, force threshold or protein mechanism.
